Official statement from the UAE Attorney General on the Flydubai case.
The Omani first officer planned to carry out a suicide attack by crashing a Flydubai passenger plane into the terminal at Ben Gurion Airport. The stated objective was to cause as many casualties as possible, in a manner similar to the September 11 attacks.
The roots of his radicalization go back to 2017, when he stayed in Melbourne, Australia, for studies and began adopting extremist views.
He also gathered intelligence in preparation for the attack attempt. That collection took place on two flights to Israel and covered both the flight path and Ben Gurion Airport itself.
On the hiring question, the Attorney General's statement says the suspect met all professional and security requirements of Flydubai at the time he was taken on. The preliminary checks conducted on him revealed no signs of extremist positions or terrorist intentions.

🔍 Iran preserved most of its missile production capacity — report
Iran still holds substantial stocks of ballistic and anti-ship missiles, and retains the industrial capacity to rapidly replenish its arsenals, Bloomberg reported citing Western officials.
This assessment directly contradicts repeated claims from the White House that Iran's military production had been destroyed.
🔴 Before the war, Israel estimated Iran had roughly 2,500 ballistic missiles
🔴 Western intelligence from June assessed Iran had kept about 75% of its pre-war arsenal
🔴 Since February 28, Iran has fired at least 2,000 ballistic missiles and over 4,000 Shahed drones, per Bloomberg Economics analysis
Officials now say Iran retains enough combat potential to retaliate if the US resumes operations — and could pivot further toward asymmetric warfare.
